Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ve looped Marissa (Legal) and Vivek (SRE) to confirm specifics and set up the export. Short bullets you can share with your SOC:  

• Retention windows (default): request logs & inference traces = 90 days; audit logs (auth/admin) = 365 days.
• Forensic export availability: we can prepare an immutable export and provision a time-limited secure download for 30 days by default; retention-on-request can be extended to 1 year with a signed data retention addendum.
• Internal access: restricted to named individuals on a need-to-know basis (SRE on-call + Platform Security + Legal). I’m copying Marissa and Vivek to confirm the list and role titles for your records.
• Immutability & legal hold: exports are placed in a locked S3 prefix with server-side KMS and object lock set to 'governance' mode; standard process is to open a support ticket and sign an evidence-handling agreement if you require longer preservation.
• Backups / Archives: There are weekly cold snapshots kept for 12 months; these are separate from the active export path and require an approval workflow to access.

Next steps: Vivek to confirm the exact export contents and timeline; Marissa to confirm the wording for the retention addendum and the required signing process. I will kick off an internal ticket and share the secure download link when ready.

Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa — technical confirmation and proposed timeline:  

1) What we can export (concrete):
   - Request logs (timestamp, request id, client id, route, latency, status) — default export contains full metadata.
   - Inference traces: by default we include token-level traces only when the customer signs the data-access addendum; otherwise we provide prompt/response hashes + metadata.
   - KV cache metadata & routing headers (no embedded secrets).
   - Platform audit logs (admin actions, API key events) as separate CSVs.

2) Immutability and storage:
   - We'll stage the bundle in an evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/acme/incident-20270409/
   - KMS encryption + S3 Object Lock (governance mode) applied; object manifest: evidence_export_manifest.csv (attached).
   - Default public-facing download expiration: 30 days. We can apply a retention tag to extend to 365 days at Acme's request.

3) Backups & archives:
   - Weekly cold snapshots exist in a separate archive account; those are kept 12 months and require an access request with approval from Platform Security and Legal.

4) Access list (internal):
   - Vivek Kulkarni (SRE Lead) — access to raw bundle for export generation.
   - Karthik Iyer (Solutions) — customer liaison and approval.
   - Marissa Cole (Legal) — review & custody approval.
   - Access will be logged and time-limited; any external download will be tracked by pre-signed URL.

5) PII handling & scrubbing:
   - If Acme requests token-level content, we will require a signed data-access addendum. We can also produce a redacted export where candidate PII (emails, SSNs) is hashed or removed — this reduces forensic fidelity.

Timeline & next steps:
   - Prep export: 24-48 hours from approval.
   - Evidence staged & manifest posted: will provide secure Drive link + S3 presigned URL.
   - If Acme signs retention addendum, we set retention tag to 365 days; otherwise default 30 days.

Attachments: evidence_export_manifest.csv (contains file list and checksums), forensic_access_timeline.txt (proposed access window).

If Marissa confirms legal wording, I’ll start the export and drop the secure link into the Jira ticket SEC-4521.
